clue.text: We hear male is not in suitable clothing

indicators.note: the male pronoun is not in the phrase any more, so those letters are taken out of it

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone overhears that a man is not dressed properly for the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking HE out of WEHEAR leaves the answer; 'We hear' looks like a homophone signal but is the fodder itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear is used for clothing suited to an occasion, as in evening wear or sportswear.

clue.text: Treaty reportedly in the bag after battle was over

indicators.note: after places the bag piece behind the battle piece

parts.note: war is fighting on a large scale

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word was is written backwards
reportedly says the phrase is taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: packed means put in the bag

explanation.surface: A peace treaty is said to be settled once the fighting has stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns PACKED into PACT by sound; 'over' reverses WAS to SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The Warsaw Pact was the 1955 mutual defence treaty of the Soviet bloc.

clue.text: Kind and friendly? A fine tale!

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a fable is a short moral tale

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims sarcastically at a story that is supposedly pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable describes someone genial and easy to talk to, kind and friendly.

clue.text: Writer gambles on a page being sufficient for additional sections

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it, so the writer and gambles come after the page

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to dice is to gamble with dice

explanation.surface: An author bets that one page will be enough for the extra material in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being sufficient for' is the link between wordplay and definition: the pieces suffice to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Appendices are supplementary sections added at the end of a book or report.

clue.text: Chief steward bringing in tea for a customer

indicators.note: bringing in means the steward's word takes the drink inside it

parts.note: a purser is the officer in charge of money and stewards on a ship
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A head steward serves tea to a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchaser is a buyer, and a customer is someone who buys.

clue.text: Consumer society unacceptable in holy festival

indicators.note: the society letter is unacceptable and so is thrown out of the festival

parts.note: Easter is the Christian festival of the resurrection

explanation.surface: Consumer culture is out of place during a sacred holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer society' reads as one phrase, but 'Consumer' is the definition and 'society' the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is one who consumes food, hence a consumer.

clue.text: The way of the British government

definitions.text: The way of the British government

parts.words: The way of the British government
parts.note: reads as the government's manner of doing things, but way means a road: the street housing the Prime Minister

explanation.definitionFit: Downing Street is the London road where the Prime Minister lives and works, so it stands for the government.

clue.text: Initially content to stay behind, one's not easily shaken off

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word content

parts.note: to linger is to remain after others go

explanation.surface: Someone happy to stay on is hard to get rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinger holds on tightly, a person or thing that is hard to shake loose.

clue.text: Love to enter revue after dropping wife off — here?

indicators.note: to enter means the love letter goes into the shortened show
after dropping means once a letter has been let go from the word
off says the wife letter is taken off

parts.note: a revue is a show of sketches and songs
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic goes to a revue once his wife has left.
explanation.walkthrough: SOHO is a London district famous for theatres, revues and nightlife, hence 'here?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is the West End area known for shows and revues, the place the surface pictures.

clue.text: One won't accept drug addict being exposed by judge

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a game
a user is slang for someone who takes drugs

explanation.surface: A judge unmasks an addict who turns down an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being exposed by' only places the judge beside the addict; it adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refuses is one who declines or will not accept something offered.

clue.text: Inspector that failed to make additional concession

indicators.note: failed means the words broke down, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inspector who did not grant an extra allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch a point is an idiom for allowing more than the rules strictly permit.

clue.text: After redevelopment, this now is just like Blackpool

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds something into a new form, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Renovation has made a place resemble an English seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: BLACKPOOL is a large seaside town in Lancashire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Townish means characteristic of a town, and Blackpool is a typical example of one.

clue.text: Opera character needed breather, perhaps, about start of long Wagner cycle

indicators.note: the jumbled breather goes about, round, the single letter taken from long
perhaps hints that the word breather is only one version of its letters, so they are rearranged
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Wagner's four-opera cycle is known as the Ring

explanation.surface: A singer playing an operatic role needs a rest before tackling Wagner's long cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges BREATHER to ABERTHER, and 'about' puts L inside it after the A. ALBERT HERRING is the title character of Britten's comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Herring is the title role of Benjamin Britten's comic opera, a character in an opera.

clue.text: Approving merger of nine states

indicators.note: a merger blends parts together, so the letters of the phrase are mixed

explanation.surface: Several states agree to unite.
explanation.definitionFit: Assentient is a formal adjective meaning assenting or agreeing, so approving.

clue.text: Sheep finally allowed round a: fold

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word sheep
the word for allowed goes round the letter a, enclosing it

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A farmer permits sheep to go round a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' looks like a sheep pen in this farming picture, but it is a crease in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed or stitched into fabric.

clue.text: Idlers shot by noisy soldiers

parts.note: a slug is a bullet, or a shot of spirits

indicators.note: noisy says the word is to be taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: guards are soldiers, as in the Grenadier Guards

explanation.surface: Lazy people are gunned down by loud troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisy' signals that GUARDS is spelt by its sound, GARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggards are lazy, slow-moving people, idlers by another name.

clue.text: Showing little emotion, peace keepers left, having secured front of castle

parts.note: UN peacekeepers belong to the United Nations

indicators.note: secured means held inside, so the word for left takes in the letter

parts.note: exited means left or went out

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Calmly, the peacekeepers withdrew after taking the castle gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Unexcited means calm and unmoved, displaying little feeling.

clue.text: Toy firm manufactured shocker

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up anew, so the letters of shocker are reworked

explanation.surface: A toy company has produced something truly dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: COCKHORSE, a hobby horse, is familiar from the nursery rhyme 'Ride a cock-horse to Banbury Cross'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockhorse is a child's rocking horse or hobby horse, a plaything.

clue.text: Fine wine producer's task?

definitions.meaning: old British slang for excellent, splendid
putting the corks into bottles is a job for a winemaker

explanation.definitionFit: Corking is slang for excellent and also the act of stopping bottles with corks.

clue.text: After meal, find ends of spare rib

indicators.note: after places the ends of spare behind the meal

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Once dinner is over, look for the remains of a spare rib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rib' sits in a food picture with 'spare', but it is the verb meaning to make fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to tease them in a good-humoured way.

clue.text: Typical building society customer loses capital over time

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second
losing its capital means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a saver keeps money in a building society, a British savings bank
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: An ordinary building society member's money loses value over time.
explanation.walkthrough: A building society is a British mutual savings and mortgage lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means normal or typical, of the usual standard.

clue.text: Delighted to involve pro-revolutionary soldiers in move towards peace?

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the word for delighted enfolds the other pieces

parts.note: rapt means enraptured, delighted
taken as written
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
men are soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A peace move pleases someone keen to draw in soldiers who back the revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to involve' puts the three short pieces inside the word for delighted, between its third and fourth letters; 'pro-revolutionary' splits across its hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapprochement is the re-establishment of friendly relations, a step towards peace between parties.

clue.text: Raise animals — notably cattle — here, primarily

definitions.text: Raise animals — notably cattle — here, primarily

indicators.note: primarily, in the first place, picks the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Animals, chiefly cattle, are bred at this place.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm where cattle or other animals are raised.

clue.text: Benefit brought by pioneer out east

indicators.note: out says the east letter is put out of the name

parts.note: Daniel Boone was a famous American frontier pioneer
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An early settler brings good things from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or benefit.

clue.text: Head accepts religious belief

indicators.note: one word accepts, takes in, the other piece

parts.note: onion is old slang for the head, as in off one's onion
pi, short for pious, means religious

explanation.surface: A leader takes on a religious creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a leader, but it is the old slang for the head, which 'accepts' the short religious abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief held about something.

clue.text: Carry out scientific analysis to reveal speed of bird

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A scientist runs tests to measure how fast a bird flies.
explanation.definitionFit: To titrate is to determine a concentration by chemical analysis, adding a reagent until a reaction completes.

clue.text: Plant giving protection from the moon's brightness?

definitions.text: Plant giving protection from the moon's brightness?

parts.words: Plant giving protection from the moon's brightness?
parts.note: read whimsically as a shade worn at night against moonlight, but it names a poisonous plant family

explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade and its relatives are plants, and the name splits into a night-time screen.

clue.text: Criminal tendency

explanation.definitionFit: Bent means corrupt in slang and also a natural inclination, two separate senses.
